what: The URL Slug Generator turns a title or phrase into a clean slug: the short, readable part of a web address, like how-to-bake-bread.

It removes accents, punctuation and emoji, and turns other alphabets into Latin letters, so titles in Russian, Greek, Arabic, Hindi, Thai, Korean, Japanese kana and Chinese become readable addresses. Or keep your own letters with a Unicode slug.
You can make one slug or thousands at once, with your choice of separator, length and case.
uses: Make tidy addresses for new articles in any content system.
Create product and category addresses from product names in several languages.
Paste a column of titles from a spreadsheet and download the matching slugs as CSV.
Turn titles into safe file or folder names without spaces or special characters.
Check what slugs your code should produce for tricky titles.
tutorial: Type or paste your title. The slug appears as you type.
Hyphens are the usual choice for web addresses; underscores or dots are also available.
Set Maximum length (80 by default; 0 means no limit). With Cut at a whole word, the slug never ends in half a word.
Lowercase, removing short common words, German-style umlauts (ä → ae) and keeping non-Latin letters are all optional.
Type your site address, such as https://example.com/blog/, to see the full link.
Put one title per line. Repeated slugs get -2, -3 so every one is unique. Copy all or download a CSV with titles and slugs.
features: Cyrillic (with the right rules for Russian, Ukrainian, Bulgarian, Serbian and more), Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Thai, Korean, Japanese kana and Chinese pinyin.
Accents removed, apostrophes dropped (don't → dont), & written as and (or your own word), no double or trailing separators.
Keep letters of any language for sites that support international addresses.
Cuts at a whole word so slugs stay readable.
Thousands of slugs at once, unique, with a CSV download that opens in Excel.

example.title: A French title
example.text: Type: Crème brûlée & café: 10 recettes faciles! The slug is creme-brulee-and-cafe-10-recettes-faciles. Change Write & as to et for creme-brulee-et-cafe-10-recettes-faciles, or tick Remove short common words to drop words like et and de.

tips: Shorter slugs are easier to share; 3 to 6 words is plenty.
Avoid changing a slug after a page is published; old links will break unless you add a redirect.
Use hyphens rather than underscores: search engines treat hyphens as word separators.
For Ukrainian, Serbian or Bulgarian titles, set Cyrillic as to that language for the official spelling.
Unicode slugs look nice in the address bar but become long %-codes when copied into some apps.
problems: The title has no letters or digits, only symbols or emoji. Add some words.
Kanji need a dictionary to read and are left out. Write those words in kana or Latin letters.
